text:
For two periods at TD Garden, nobody could separate these teams. Then Boston scored three times in 75 seconds of game time late in the third, and a scoreless game turned into a 3-0 result that was easy to read as a rout. Fraser Minten snapped one home at 16:14, JJ Peterka did the same at 17:06, and Mark Kastelic finished it at 17:29 on a 76 percent chance, the only one of the three that was a true gimme.

The ice was tilted toward Boston in the end, but not by as much as the score says. The Bruins out-chanced the Rangers 3.38 expected goals to 2.01 and took 55 shot attempts to 47, which gave them a 61 percent share of simulated replays. The second period was nearly even (BOS 0.97, NYR 0.93), and the third is where the gap opened, 1.78 to 0.71. Minten was on the ice for 1.27 expected goals for and 0.60 against, and Hampus Lindholm finished at 2.02 to 0.60.

The quieter story was Jeremy Swayman. He stopped all 24 shots, about two goals better than the chances he faced deserved, including Eeli Tolvanen's 21 percent look in the second period. Igor Shesterkin saved 20 of 22 and was roughly a goal-saved better than average, which makes the margin harder to blame on him. Boston also gave the puck away 10 times to New York's 20, a small but telling edge in a game that stayed tight until it didn't.
